fullPassage:
Artificial Intelligence and the Arts

On March 13, 2016, an incident occurred that thrilled the contemporary art scene. An unknown painting that seemed to be a work of Rembrandt, the great 17th-century Dutch painter, had been discovered! Rembrandt experts from all over the world gathered to view this portrait of a middle-aged man. They immediately recognized the artist's vivid style, but thoroughly examined the painting to make sure. Several hours later, they confirmed, "This is a genuine Rembrandt." How wonderful to greet a new work of this extraordinary artist more than 300 years after his death!

Suddenly, a group of people appeared in front of them. Their representative announced, "This is not a genuine work of Rembrandt." The experts protested, "With these features of brush and paint, this painting cannot be any other artist's work!" The representative calmly explained, "This painting was created by an artificial intelligence system through 3D printing. We are the engineers who developed that AI system."

The experts asked them to offer some evidence. They immediately presented a video showing the AI's production process. Their AI program learned to imitate Rembrandt's typical characteristics by examining data from his 346 works. It was then given the order "Make a portrait of a Caucasian male, 30 to 40 years old, with facial hair, in dark clothing with a collar, wearing a hat, and facing to the right" and produced what seemed to be a genuine Rembrandt. The experts were stunned.

This was just one of the events that provoked the question: "Can AI art be real art?" This question is unresolved, but more and more art critics see AI-generated artworks as a new field of art, just as photography eventually came to be seen as art rather than technology more than a century ago.

In 2018, a portrait created by AI was sold for nearly half a million dollars. The painting, Portrait of Edmond de Belamy, was produced by an art group, using an algorithm and a data bank of 15,000 portraits. This sale helped AI artworks become more accepted in the traditional art world. In 2022, an AI-generated picture, Théâtre D'opéra Spatial, won first prize in the Colorado State Fair's art contest. Since then, more and more AI-generated artworks have been exhibited in art galleries.

There are different views of AI art. To many people, it is at best an imitation of human art, not a true art form with insight into life and society. Some oppose AI-generated art because it can steal the data of human art without respecting copyright. In contrast, some artists welcome AI as a tool to create new art forms. There are also those who insist that AI is more than a tool. They argue that the results of AI creation are largely beyond human control and AI should therefore be seen as existing in its own right.

Let us look at the mechanism of AI creativity, which is programmed to work in a similar way to human creativity. Think of the AI technology of neural networks. It makes a machine "think," distinguish, and create in a similar way to a human brain. The machine doesn't simply follow human orders but learns by itself, which is done through a branch of machine learning called deep learning. This learning process enables a machine to discover distinct patterns from numerous data. Moreover, AI can even learn established art styles only to avoid them. It can then create a new, unique style.

This pattern of AI creation is much like the path taken by major artists such as Picasso and Van Gogh. These artists trained themselves by learning and mimicking other artists' styles until they found and created their own.

Of course, this does not mean that an AI system becomes an artist in the same way that a human does. Human artistic creativity, which raises ethical, social, or emotional questions through great art, is not yet thoroughly understood and cannot simply be compared with any AI system. Even so, we have better and better AI techniques which are able to imitate human creative activities. AI has already generated art that some viewers consider more impressive or moving than human art.

Now, we see AI platforms and apps that create pictures, music albums, and novels if we simply provide them with an idea. Although our question, "Can AI art be real art?", is still valid, AI can be a powerful source of inspiration and ideas for artists. AI-generated art will continue to challenge our views on creativity in the arts and the human relationship with machine intelligence.

questions.passage: Suddenly, a group of people appeared in front of them. Their representative ①<u>announced</u>, "This is not a genuine work of Rembrandt." The experts ②<u>protested</u>, "With these features of brush and paint, this painting cannot be any other artist's work!" The representative calmly explained, "This painting ③<u>was created</u> by an artificial intelligence system. We are the engineers ④<u>whom</u> developed that AI system."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 그 AI 시스템을 개발한 엔지니어들입니다. who가 주격 관계대명사.
det.analysis: ✅ ①announced: 과거형 정상. ✅ ②protested: 과거형 정상. ✅ ③was created: 수동태 정상. ❌ ④whom: 관계대명사 뒤 동사 developed의 주어 역할 → who(주격) 필요. whom은 목적격.
det.tip: who(주격) vs whom(목적격). 뒤에 동사가 바로 오면 who. the engineers who developed (O).

questions.passage: This was just one of the events that provoked the question. More and more art critics see AI-generated artworks as a new field of art, just as photography eventually ①<u>came</u> to be seen as art rather than technology. In 2018, a portrait ②<u>created</u> by AI was sold for nearly half a million dollars. The painting was produced by an art group, using an algorithm and a data bank of 15,000 portraits. This sale helped AI artworks ③<u>to become</u> more accepted. Since then, more and more artworks ④<u>have been exhibited</u> in art galleries.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 판매는 AI 예술 작품이 더 인정받게 도왔다. help + O + 원형부정사.
det.analysis: ✅ ①came: 과거형 정상. ✅ ②created: 과거분사 수동 정상. ❌ ③to become: 원문은 help + O + 원형부정사(become). 'helped AI artworks become'이 원문. ✅ ④have been exhibited: since then + 현재완료 정상.
det.tip: help + O + V(원형) 또는 help + O + to V 둘 다 가능하나, 원문은 become(원형). 시험에서는 원문 기준.

questions.passage: The machine doesn't simply follow human orders but learns by itself, which is done through a branch of machine learning ①<u>called</u> deep learning. This learning process enables a machine ②<u>to discover</u> distinct patterns from numerous data. AI can even learn ③<u>established</u> art styles only to avoid them. These artists trained themselves by learning and mimicking other artists' styles until they ④<u>found and creating</u> their own.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 예술가들은 자신만의 스타일을 찾고 창조할 때까지. found and created — 병렬.
det.analysis: ✅ ①called: 과거분사(수동). ✅ ②to discover: enable + O + to V. ✅ ③established: 과거분사 형용사(확립된). ❌ ④found and creating: 병렬 구조 위반. found(과거)와 creating(동명사) 혼용. found and created가 올바름.
det.tip: 병렬 구조: found and created (과거+과거). found and creating (과거+동명사) = 구조 불일치.

questions.passage: On March 13, 2016, an incident occurred that thrilled the contemporary art scene. An unknown painting had been discovered! Rembrandt experts from all over the world gathered to view this portrait. They immediately recognized the artist's vivid style. Suddenly, a group of people appeared. Their representative ①<u>announced</u>, "This is not a genuine work of Rembrandt." The experts ②<u>protested</u>. The representative calmly ③<u>explained</u> that the painting was created by AI. The experts asked them to ④<u>conceal</u> some evidence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전문가들은 증거를 제시해 달라고(offer) 요청했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①announced(발표했다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②protested(항의했다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③explained(설명했다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④conceal(숨기다): 원문은 offer(제시하다). 증거를 숨기라는 것은 문맥 반대.
det.tip: offer(제시하다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). 전문가들이 증거를 '요구'하는 맥락.

questions.passage: Let us look at the mechanism of AI creativity. Think of the AI technology of neural networks. It makes a machine "think," distinguish, and create in a similar way to a human brain. The machine doesn't simply follow human orders but learns by itself, which is done through a branch of machine learning called deep learning. This learning process enables a machine to discover ①<u>distinct</u> patterns from ②<u>numerous</u> data. Moreover, AI can even learn ③<u>established</u> art styles only to ④<u>embrace</u> them. It can then create a new, unique style.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: AI는 확립된 미술 양식을 배워서 피하기(avoid) 위해서만 학습한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①distinct(뚜렷한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②numerous(수많은): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③established(확립된): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④embrace(수용하다): 원문은 avoid(피하다). 기존 스타일을 피해 새로운 스타일을 만드는 맥락.
det.tip: avoid(피하다) ↔ embrace(수용하다). 'only to avoid' = 결과적으로 피하기 위해. 새 스타일 창조의 전제.

questions.passage: There are different views of AI art. To many people, it is at best an imitation of human art, not a true art form with insight into life and society. Some oppose AI-generated art because it can __________ without respecting copyright. In contrast, some artists welcome AI as a tool to create new art forms.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: steal the data of human art
improve the quality of copyright law

det.korean: 저작권을 존중하지 않고 인간 예술의 데이터를 훔칠 수 있기 때문이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①steal the data of human art: oppose(반대)의 이유 + without respecting copyright과 연결. ❌ ②improve copyright law: 반대 이유가 아님. ❌ ③promote original works: 문맥 반대. ❌ ④increase respect: oppose와 모순.
det.tip: oppose + because + steal + without respecting copyright: 반대 이유 구조.

questions.passage: This pattern of AI creation is much like the path taken by major artists such as Picasso and Van Gogh. These artists trained themselves by learning and mimicking other artists' styles until they found and created their own. Of course, this does not mean that an AI system becomes an artist __________. Human artistic creativity is not yet thoroughly understood and cannot simply be compared with any AI system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: faster than any human artist ever could
without using any data or algorithms
in the same way that a human does

det.korean: AI 시스템이 인간과 같은 방식으로 예술가가 되는 것을 의미하지 않는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④in the same way that a human does: 뒤에 human creativity를 단순 비교할 수 없다는 내용과 연결. ❌ ①faster: 속도 비교 아님. ❌ ②replacing galleries: 언급 없음. ❌ ③without data: 사실과 반대.
det.tip: in the same way that = ~와 같은 방식으로. does not mean + 빈칸 → 부정 내용.

questions.passage: On March 13, 2016, an incident occurred that thrilled the contemporary art scene. An unknown painting that seemed to be a work of Rembrandt, the great 17th-century Dutch painter, had been discovered! Rembrandt experts from all over the world gathered to view this portrait of a middle-aged man. They immediately recognized the artist's vivid style. Several hours later, they confirmed, "This is a genuine Rembrandt."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 전 세계의 렘브란트 전문가들이 초상화를 보기 위해 모였다.
전문가들은 그 그림이 가짜라고 즉시 판단했다.

det.korean: 전 세계의 렘브란트 전문가들이 중년 남성의 초상화를 보기 위해 모였다.
det.analysis: ❌ ①2016년(O), 2018년(X). ✅ ②from all over the world gathered — 일치. ❌ ③middle-aged man(O), 젊은 여성(X). ❌ ④진품이라고 확인(O), 가짜(X).
det.tip: 숫자/연도 변조와 인물 특성 변조 주의. 2016 vs 2018, middle-aged man vs young woman.

questions.passage: Their AI program learned to imitate Rembrandt's typical characteristics by examining data from his 346 works. It was then given the order "Make a portrait of a Caucasian male, 30 to 40 years old, with facial hair, in dark clothing with a collar, wearing a hat, and facing to the right" and produced what seemed to be a genuine Rembrandt.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: AI 프로그램은 렘브란트의 전형적인 특징을 모방하는 법을 배웠다.
AI에게 50대 여성의 초상화를 만들라는 명령이 주어졌다.
AI가 만든 작품은 진품 렘브란트처럼 보였다.

det.korean: AI에게 주어진 명령은 30~40세 백인 남성의 초상화. 50대 여성이 아님.
det.analysis: ✅ ①일치: learned to imitate. ✅ ②일치: 346 works. ❌ ③불일치: 30 to 40 years old Caucasian male(O), 50대 여성(X). ✅ ④일치: seemed to be a genuine Rembrandt.
det.tip: 30 to 40 years old / Caucasian male — 나이와 성별 변조 주의.

questions.passage: There are different views of AI art. To many people, it is at best an imitation of human art, not a true art form with insight into life and society. Some oppose AI-generated art because it can steal the data of human art without respecting copyright. In contrast, some artists welcome AI as a tool to create new art forms. There are also those who insist that AI is more than a tool. They argue that the results of AI creation are largely beyond human control and AI should therefore be seen as existing in its own right.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 모든 사람이 AI 예술을 진정한 예술로 인정한다.
AI 반대론자들은 AI가 저작권을 보호한다고 주장한다.
일부 사람들은 AI가 도구 이상이라고 주장한다.
AI 창작의 결과는 전적으로 인간의 통제 하에 있다.

det.korean: 일부는 AI가 도구 이상이라고 주장하며, AI 창작은 대부분 인간 통제 너머라고 한다.
det.analysis: ❌ ①'모든 사람'이 아닌 'different views'. ❌ ②steal without respecting copyright(저작권 침해). ✅ ③insist that AI is more than a tool — 일치. ❌ ④largely beyond human control(대부분 통제 밖).
det.tip: beyond human control = 인간 통제 밖. in its own right = 그 자체로.

questions.passage: On March 13, 2016, an incident occurred that thrilled the contemporary art scene. An unknown painting that seemed to be a work of Rembrandt had been discovered! Several hours later, experts confirmed it as genuine. But then a group announced the painting was created by AI through 3D printing. This was just one of the events that provoked the question: "Can AI art be real art?" This question is unresolved, but more and more art critics see AI-generated artworks as a new field of art.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: AI 예술이 진짜 예술인지에 대한 논쟁의 시작

det.korean: AI가 렘브란트 스타일의 그림을 만든 사건을 통해 'AI 예술이 진짜 예술인가?'라는 질문이 촉발되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②AI 예술의 진위 논쟁 시작. ❌ ①미발견 작품이 아닌 AI 작품. ❌ ③3D 프린팅 산업이 주제 아님. ❌ ④17세기 회화 자체가 아닌 AI 모방.
det.tip: 주제 = provoked the question + unresolved. 논쟁의 시작이 핵심.

questions.passage: Let us look at the mechanism of AI creativity, which is programmed to work in a similar way to human creativity. The machine doesn't simply follow human orders but learns by itself through deep learning. This learning process enables a machine to discover distinct patterns from numerous data. Moreover, AI can even learn established art styles only to avoid them. It can then create a new, unique style. This pattern of AI creation is much like the path taken by major artists such as Picasso and Van Gogh.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: AI 창의성의 메커니즘: 인간 예술가와의 유사성
피카소와 반 고흐의 초기 작품 분석

det.korean: AI 창의성의 메커니즘이 인간 창의성과 유사하게 작동하며, 피카소/반 고흐의 경로와 비슷하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①mechanism of AI creativity + much like major artists. ❌ ②딥러닝 실패 언급 없음. ❌ ③초기 작품 분석이 아님. ❌ ④인간 두뇌 자체가 주제 아님.
det.tip: 제목 = 글 전체를 포괄하는 핵심어. mechanism + similar to human creativity.

questions.passage: This question is unresolved, but more and more art critics see AI-generated artworks as a new field of art, just as <u>photography eventually came to be seen as art rather than technology</u> more than a century ago. AI-generated art will continue to challenge our views on creativity in the arts.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 처음에는 기술로 여겨졌던 것이 결국 예술로 인정받을 수 있다.
AI 예술은 사진처럼 곧 사라질 것이다.
한 세기 전의 예술이 현대보다 우수했다.

det.korean: 사진이 기술에서 예술로 인정받은 것처럼, AI 예술도 그럴 수 있다는 가능성을 시사.
det.analysis: ✅ ②사진 사례 = AI 예술도 같은 경로를 밟을 수 있다는 함축. ❌ ①사진은 이미 예술로 인정. ❌ ③사라진다는 언급 없음. ❌ ④우열 비교 아님.
det.tip: just as A, so B: A처럼 B도. 유추(analogy) 표현. photography → AI art.

questions.passage: Suddenly, a group of people appeared in front of them. Their representative announced, "This is not a genuine work of Rembrandt." The experts protested. The representative calmly explained, "This painting was created by an artificial intelligence system through 3D printing. We are the engineers who developed that AI system." The experts asked <u>them</u> to offer some evidence.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전문가들이 엔지니어 그룹에게 증거를 제시해 달라고 요청했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③a group of people = the engineers. experts가 them(엔지니어들)에게 증거를 요구. ❌ ①experts가 experts에게 증거 요구 → 비논리. ❌ ②그림들에게 증거 요구 불가. ❌ ④관람객 언급 없음.
det.tip: them = a group of people = the engineers who developed that AI system.

questions.passage: This pattern of AI creation is much like the path taken by major artists such as Picasso and Van Gogh. These artists trained themselves by learning and mimicking other artists' styles until they found and created their own. Of course, this does not mean that an AI system becomes an artist in the same way that a human does. Human artistic creativity, which raises ethical, social, or emotional questions through great art, is not yet thoroughly understood and cannot simply be compared with any AI system. Even so, we have better and better AI techniques which are able to imitate <u>it</u>.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: AI 기술은 인간의 창의적 활동을 모방할 수 있다. 원문은 'imitate human creative activities'.
det.analysis: ✅ ①human creative activities를 대명사 it으로 받음. 바로 앞 문장에서 human artistic creativity를 언급하고, AI가 그것을 imitate한다는 맥락. ❌ ②AI 기술 자체를 모방하는 것이 아님. ❌ ③렘브란트는 이 문단의 주제가 아님. ❌ ④심사 기준 언급 없음.
det.tip: it = human creative activities (원문 참조). imitate + 목적어 관계.

questions.passage: In 2018, a portrait created by AI was sold for nearly half a million dollars. The painting, Portrait of Edmond de Belamy, was produced by an art group, using an algorithm and a data bank of 15,000 portraits. This sale helped AI artworks become more accepted in the traditional art world. In 2022, an AI-generated picture, Théâtre D'opéra Spatial, won first prize in the Colorado State Fair's art contest.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Portrait of Edmond de Belamy는 알고리즘과 15,000장의 초상화 데이터 뱅크를 사용하여 한 예술 그룹이 __________ 한 것이다."

det.korean: 한 예술 그룹이 제작한(produced) 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ produced: 원문 'was produced by an art group'에서 발췌.

Even so, we have better and better AI techniques which are able to imitate human creative activities. AI has already generated art that some viewers consider more impressive or moving than human art.
